observation.coverage_basis: Receives already-instrumented OTLP logs and spans. The recorder preserves supported metadata, removes fields outside exact allowlists, and routes accepted activity, but cannot reconstruct semantics that upstream instrumentation did not emit.

authentication.credential_handling: Outbound header and TLS credentials can be mounted from operator-created Kubernetes Secrets or Compose secrets; bearer-token ingress is wired by the compose production overlay and mTLS by the production Helm profile.

correlation_limitations: The receiver preserves correlation present in OTLP but cannot repair absent or incorrectly parented spans.
Trace identity attributes are asserted by the sender and are not bound to ingress workload identity.
Trace identity (trace_id, span_id, parent linkage) is preserved; free-form tracestate payloads on spans and links are cleared at export because they are caller-controlled text.

verification_evidence.claim: Verifies that logs and traces are forced through the exact-key allowlist and that legacy control, redaction, and sampling surfaces cannot render.
Verifies persistent queue, retry, TLS, and authentication configuration gates.

known_blind_spots: The pinned bearertokenauth extension (v0.150.0) splits token files on newlines and retains empty entries, so a blank line or trailing newline mints an empty "Bearer " credential that gRPC metadata preserves; preflight-prod.sh rejects unsafe files, fabric-gate refuses them at boot and while running (the extension re-reads via fsnotify), verify-prod.sh re-checks them, and an upstream patch is prepared under components/otel-collector-fabric/upstream/.
The production chart supports mTLS ingress, but does not bind asserted telemetry identity attributes to a verified workload identity.
The receiver cannot observe agent activity that was never emitted by upstream instrumentation.

Shipped configurations are limited to traces and logs pipelines; the fabric-gate image entrypoint refuses to boot a config defining any other pipeline, and qualify-distribution-config.sh proves the refusal. Operators who build or wrap their own collector binary lose that enforcement and must re-apply the qualification gate.
Bounded free-form caller metadata, including interaction kinds and tool names, crosses the boundary verbatim and is not semantic content; destinations should treat it as asserted-unverified metadata.
The recorder preserves protected OTLP and does not materialize Activity Envelope v2, privacy assertions, or delivery receipts; a downstream adapter or destination must provide those contracts.
The default development exporter is local stdout, not durable evidence storage or a compliance posture; the production profile requires an authenticated TLS destination.
Persistent queues provide bounded at-least-once transport and cannot prove backend retention or exactly-once delivery.
Metadata allowlisting occurs after the agent and model interaction and cannot prevent raw PII from reaching an LLM.
